parts.label: a
parts.reason: No statement in the specification list covers momentum conservation or collisions (PCLM); M8 statements only cover Newton's laws, forces, friction, pulleys - not impact/momentum. This topic is absent from every statement.

parts.label: b
parts.reason: Impulse and momentum are not mentioned in any 9MA0 statement (only force, weight, moment listed as derived quantities in M6.1); this is out of spec and also depends on part (a).

parts.label: a
parts.technique: suvat - motion under gravity, greatest height
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae for straight line motion; M8.3 covers weight and motion under gravity with g constant. Standard projectile vertical motion is covered.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: suvat with quadratic in t, time above a height
parts.reason: Uses constant acceleration formulae (M7.3) and motion under gravity (M8.3); solving resulting quadratic is standard algebra (P2.3). Fully in spec.

parts.label: (i)+(ii)
parts.technique: Equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces (resolving)
parts.reason: M8.4 explicitly covers equilibrium of a particle under coplanar forces, resolving forces in 2 dimensions - directly matches this tension problem.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: M8.2/M8.4 cover Newton's second law for straight-line motion and connected particle problems including lift problems explicitly mentioned in M8.4 guidance.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Newton's second law applied to whole system (cable force)
parts.reason: Same as above - system/lift dynamics covered by M8.2 and M8.4 guidance on lift problems.

parts.label: (a)(i)+(ii)
parts.technique: Moments in static context (beam with two ropes)
parts.reason: M9.1 explicitly covers moments in simple static contexts, including problems with parallel coplanar forces.

parts.label: (b)(i)+(ii)
parts.technique: Moments - finding greatest value / tension range
parts.reason: Continues the moments problem from M9.1; finding constraints (tension non-negative) is standard application of moments equilibrium.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: M7.3/M7.4 cover use of vectors in kinematics including position vector r; simple substitution of t=0.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Solving for time using vector position equation
parts.reason: Matching components of the vector position equation, covered under M7.3/M7.4 vector kinematics with i-j notation, plus P10 vector algebra.

parts.label: c
parts.reason: M7.4 covers differentiation of position vector to get velocity in 2D, and P10.2 covers magnitude of a vector; fully in spec.

parts.label: a
parts.reason: M7.2 explicitly covers interpreting and using graphs in kinematics including velocity-time graphs.

parts.label: (b)(i)-(iii)
parts.technique: Using constant acceleration formulae to find times in terms of V
parts.reason: M7.3 covers constant acceleration formulae for straight-line motion, directly applicable to finding times of acceleration/deceleration/constant speed phases.

parts.label: c
parts.technique: Using area under v-t graph (trapezium) to solve for V via quadratic
parts.reason: M7.2 covers area under velocity-time graph representing distance; solving resulting quadratic is standard algebra (P2.3). In spec.

parts.label: a
parts.technique: Connected particles, pulley, inclined plane with friction
parts.reason: M8.4 guidance explicitly includes connected particle problems with smooth pulleys and at least one particle on an inclined plane; M8.6 covers friction (F ≤ μR model). Fully matches.

parts.label: b
parts.technique: Resultant force on pulley from string tensions (resolving forces)
parts.reason: This uses vector addition/resolution of two tension forces at an angle to find resultant magnitude - covered by general force resolution principles under M8.4/M8.5 (addition of forces, resultant forces).
